confirmed_items.evidence: C:/Dropbox/Research/ai-lab/literature/creativity/Shin et al (2025) - No Evidence for LLMs Being Useful in Problem Reframing.pdf; PDF p. 6, Figure 4, labels the randomized designers N = 456 and states that each participant was randomly assigned an approach. verdict.correct_value: Of 456 designers randomized to reframe a design problem without an LLM or with GPT-4o in three ways, 280 were analyzed, and rater-scored novelty and usefulness of the frame each person picked as best did not differ between MANUAL (62 analyzed) and LLM-ALL (218 analyzed) or among the four approaches (all p > 0.05), reported only as box plots (p. 6, Figure 4 and Section 4.2; p. 8, Figure 5; pp. 8-9, Section 5.2).

verdict.correct_value: Figures 2a and 2b have error bars the paper does not define; participant-level arm SDs or SEs for the creativity scores are not printed (pp. 8-12 and 28-30). Tables 4a and 4b do report standard deviations of the projected semantic embeddings (pp. 16-17). Participant-level arm SDs of creativity scores are the preferred standardizer (codebook section 9).
verdict.evidence: C:/Users/German/Dropbox/Admin/website/ai-skill-atlas/docs/creativity-screening-2026-10-04.md, line 1312, contains the blanket statement that no SDs or SEs are printed anywhere. Directly inspected C:/Dropbox/Research/ai-lab/literature/creativity/Liu et al (2024) - When ChatGPT is Gone Creativity Reverts and Homogeneity Persists.pdf using PyMuPDF: PDF p. 17, Table 4a, explicitly labels Standard Deviation columns for Control and GPT, with Day 2 values 0.40 and 0.33 and Day 30 values 0.39 and 0.32. The correction therefore belongs in the form. creativity-codebook.md, section 9, specifies participant-level control-arm and pooled-arm SDs as the preferred standardizers.
